 Judgment

1. Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 06.08.2019 passed in MVC No.1748/2017 by the Court of the II Additional District and Sessions Judge & Additional MACT, Hassan (for short 'the Tribunal'), the petitioners therein have preferred this appeal.

entities.text: II Additional District and Sessions Judge & Additional MACT, Hassan
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to herein as per their status before the Tribunal.
Brief facts of the case are as follows:

On 08.05.2017 at about 4.30 p.m. the deceased - Umesha was traveling on a motor bike bearing registration No.KA-13-EJ-5768 the said vehicle met with an accident near Gurudeva Petrol Bunk, Balegadde with a lorry bearing Reg. TN-29-AV-3488 because of which, the said Umesha expired.
The accident happened due to rash and negligent driving of the lorry, which was duly insured with respondent no.2- Insurance Company.

The Tribunal has awarded a compensation of Rs.10,07,000/-
Shanthamma vs Mubarak on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89848684/
2 along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of order till the date of realization.
Not satisfied by the same, the petitioners who are parents and brothers of the deceased have preferred this appeal.
4. The accident occurred in the year 2017.
The petitioners have not established the income of the deceased before the Tribunal.

Hence, it is deemed appropriate to fix his income notionally as per the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority NC: 2023:KHC:29386 in consultation with Insurance Companies which will be Rs.11,000/- per month.

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Services Authority NC: 2023:KHC:29386
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The deceased was aged 20 years at the time of the accident.
Hence, a multiplier of 18 is adopted as per the law laid down by the Apex Court in SARLA VERMA & ORS V. DELHI TRANSPORT CORP.& ANR reported in 2009(6) SCC 121.

entities.text: SARLA VERMA & ORS V. DELHI TRANSPORT CORP.& ANR reported in 2009(6) SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Taking the income of the deceased at Rs.11,000/- per month, 40% has to be added to his income towards future prospects as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in
NATIONAL INSURANCE CO. LTD.
V. PRANAY SETHI reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680.
As the deceased was a Bachelor, 50% is deducted towards his personal expenses.

Thus, on the count of loss of dependency, the petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.16,63,200/- (Rs.11,000/- X 12 X 18 +
40%X 1/2).
5. Petitioners are also entitled to a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards 'loss of estate and funeral expenses'.

Petitioners are all entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/- each towards 'loss of consortium' and thus together are entitled to Rs.1,60,000/- under this head.
7.
Thus, the petitioners are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.18,53,200/- as against Rs.10,07,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
Accordingly, the petitioners are together entitled to an enhanced compensation of Rs.8,46,200/- over and above what has been awarded by the Tribunal (Rs.18,53,200 minus Rs.10,07,000/-).

Of the total amount of Rs.18,53,200/-, petitioner Nos.1 and 2 being parents of the deceased are held to be entitled to a sum of Rs.17,73,200/- and petitioner Nos.3 and 4 being brother of the deceased are entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/- each along with proportionate interest thereon.
Further, given the bank rate of interest, I deem it appropriate to award interest at the rate of 6% p.a. on the enhanced compensation from the date of petition till realization.
Further, the Tribunal has awarded interest on the compensation amount granted by it at 6% per annum from the date of the order.
I find the same to be erroneous and it should be from the date of filing of the petition before the Tribunal till realization.

9. Hence, the following:
